title_en: Shijian Group Co., Ltd. v. Yuhuan County Land Bureau of Zhejiang Province — dispute over land use right grant contract
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 15, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law, an announcement for the transfer of state-owned land use rights constitutes an invitation to offer. The bidder's act of submitting a bid price in the bid application and paying the deposit in accordance with the invitation to offer constitutes an offer. At this stage, the parties have not yet formed a contract for the transfer of land use rights. If the transferor of state-owned land use rights revokes the announcement due to a violation of prohibitive provisions of the law, thereby causing the bidder to suffer reliance interest losses during the contracting phase, the transferor shall bear pre-contractual liability for the bidder's actual losses.

full_text_en:
Time Real Estate Construction Group Co., Ltd. v. Yuhuan County Land and Resources Bureau — dispute over land use right transfer contract

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to Article 15, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law, an announcement of a state-owned land use right transfer by listing constitutes an invitation to offer. The act of a bidder submitting a quotation in the bid application and paying a deposit in accordance with the invitation to offer constitutes an offer, and no contractual relationship for the transfer of the land use right has been formed between the parties. Where the transferor of a state-owned land use right, due to the transfer announcement violating the prohibitive provisions of the law, revokes the announcement, thereby causing the bidder to suffer loss of reliance interests during the contracting stage, the transferor shall bear pre-contractual liability for the bidder's actual losses.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment

(2003) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 82

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Time Real Estate Construction Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 321 Chishan East Road, Jiaojiang, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Li Weijun, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Xie Guanbin, lawyer at Beijing Cubic Law Firm.

Appellee (defendant at first instance): Yuhuan County Land and Resources Bureau, domiciled at Yuxing East Road, Chengguan, Zhugang Town, Yuhuan County, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Wuyong, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Wu Yongmin, lawyer at Zhejiang Zeda Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Huang Yan, lawyer at Beijing Tongda Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over land use right transfer contract between Time Real Estate Construction Group Co., Ltd., the appellant, and Yuhuan County Land and Resources Bureau, the appellee, the Zhejiang High People's Court rendered a civil judgment on October 24, 2003 (2003) Zhe Min Yi Chu Zi No. 1. The appellant, Time Real Estate Construction Group Co., Ltd., dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on February 9, 2004. The appellant's agent ad litem, Xie Guanbin, and the appellee's agents ad litem, Wu Yongmin and Huang Yan, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

The facts found by the first instance court upon trial:

On November 7, 2002, Yuhuan County Land and Resources Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Land Bureau) published in the "Yuhuan News" an "Announcement of Yuhuan County Land and Resources Bureau on the Listing and Transfer of State-Owned Land Use Rights" (hereinafter referred to as the "Listing Transfer Announcement"). The main contents were: Approved by the People's Government of Yuhuan County, the Land Bureau decided to list and transfer the following parcel of state-owned land use rights at the Yuhuan County Real Estate Transaction Window from 8:00 a.m. on November 21, 2002, to 3:00 p.m. on December 4, 2002: 1. The parcel is located in the reclamation development project area of Kanmen Fish Harbor Huajiaoyan, Zhugang Town, Yuhuan County, with development serial number 2002-005, area 25.9434 hectares, intended use as mixed residential land (commercial and residential mixed), land use term of 70 years; floor area ratio not exceeding 1.5, greening rate not less than 35%, sunshine spacing ratio not less than 1:1.1, building density not more than 30%, and construction to be completed within five years from the date of obtaining the land use right; 2. The starting price for the listing of this parcel is RMB 43,000,000, with 40% of the transaction price to be paid after the transaction, and the balance to be paid as stipulated in the contract; 3. Companies, enterprises, and other organizations within and outside the People's Republic of China with financial strength and the ability to complete construction within the specified time may participate in the bidding; 4. Registration period: from November 1, 2002, to 3:00 p.m. on November 20, 2002; Registration location: Yuhuan County Real Estate Transaction Window; Required documents for registration: original copy of business license with registered capital of not less than RMB 100,000,000 (with RMB 50,000,000 actually paid in), and a certificate of legal representation affixed with the company seal; 5. Bidders must pay a deposit of RMB 20,000,000 at the time of registration; 6. Listing period: from 8:00 a.m. on November 21, 2002, to 3:00 p.m. on December 4, 2002; Listing location: Yuhuan County Real Estate Transaction Window. Article 13 of the "Instructions for Listing and Transfer of State-Owned Land Use Rights of Yuhuan County Land and Resources Bureau" (hereinafter referred to as the "Listing Transfer Instructions") stated: "Upon expiry of the listing period, the transaction shall be determined according to the following provisions: (1) If there is only one bidder who has submitted a quotation during the listing period, and the quotation is higher than the reserve price and meets other conditions, the listing transaction is concluded; (2) If there are two or more bidders who have submitted quotations during the listing period, the highest bidder shall be the successful bidder; if quotations are identical, the one who submitted the quotation form first shall be the successful bidder, provided that the quotation is not lower than the reserve price; (3) If no bidder responds during the listing period, or all bidders' quotations are lower than the reserve price or fail to meet other conditions, the listing transaction is not concluded; (4) If, at the closing time of the listing period, two or more bidders still request to submit quotations, the transferor may decide to conduct an on-site auction or set another time for an auction by bidding, and the highest bidder shall be the successful bidder." On November 20, 2002, the Land Bureau received a "Listing Transfer Bid Application" from Time Real Estate Construction Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Time Company). The application stated: "Having carefully reviewed the documents of the Land Bureau for the listing and transfer of state-owned land use rights, we agree to abide by the requirements and provisions of the listing and transfer documents and decide to apply to participate in the bidding for the listing and transfer of state-owned land use rights conducted by the Land Bureau at the Yuhuan County Real Estate Exchange Window from November 21, 2002, to December 4, 2002." On the same day, Time Company remitted RMB 20,000,000 to the Yuhuan County Land Reserve Center. The Land Bureau issued a receipt for administrative and institutional current accounts of Zhejiang Province, confirming receipt of the said amount. The next day, Time Company submitted to the Land Bureau a "Listing Transfer Bid Quotation Form," quoting a price of RMB 50,000,000.

On December 14, 2001, Zhejiang Yuhui Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuhui Company) signed a "Draft Contract for the Transfer of State-Owned Land Use Rights" with the Land Bureau. Articles 4 and 7 of the contract stipulated: "The intended use of the land parcel transferred under this contract is the Sea View Garden Residential Area, the first phase of the 'Overall Development Plan for Kanmen Bay Scenic Area, Yuhuan County, Zhejiang Province (Draft)'"; "The transfer price for the land use right of the parcel under this contract is RMB 165 per square meter, totaling RMB 44,000,000." On December 18, 2001, Yuhui Company remitted RMB 1,000,000 to the Kanmen Fishing Port Development Center of Yuhuan County, Zhejiang Province, and the Center confirmed receipt of the said amount; on October 17, 2002, Yuhui Company remitted RMB 11,200,000 to the Yuhuan County Finance Bureau; on the same day, Yuhui Company remitted another RMB 2,000,000 to the Yuhuan County Finance Bureau; the next day, Yuhui Company remitted RMB 3,000,000 to the Yuhuan County Finance Bureau; on November 14, 2002, Yuhui Company submitted to the Land Bureau a "Report on Converting the Refundable Land Transfer Fee into the Land Listing Deposit," requesting that the above amounts be directly converted into the listing bid deposit; on November 18, 2002, the Land Bureau's legal representative, Wang Wuyong, agreed in writing to convert the amounts into the deposit; on November 20, 2002, Yuhui Company remitted RMB 2,800,000 to the Yuhuan County Land Reserve Center, and on the same day, the Land Bureau issued a receipt for the said amount; on November 22, 2002, the amount entered the account of the Yuhuan County Land Reserve Center; on November 21, 2002, Yuhui Company submitted to the Land Bureau a "Listing Transfer Bid Quotation Form," quoting a price of RMB 51,000,000.

On November 20, 2002, the Land Bureau deposited with the Yuhuan County Notary Office the sealed reserve price letter stating: "The reserve price for the listing and transfer of Yuhuan Seaside New City Golden Harbor (i.e., the development parcel 2002-005 in the sea area) is RMB 57,000,000, total RMB fifty-seven million yuan."

On November 20, 2002, after receiving a report that the Land Bureau had engaged in irregularities and opaque operations during the listing and transfer of the Kanmen Fishing Port Golden Bay land parcel that day, the Land Resources Department of Zhejiang Province ascertained that the parcel was being submitted for approval but had not yet been approved, and ordered the Land Bureau to stop the listing pending lawful approval. On November 22, 2002, the Land Bureau issued to Time Company and Yuhui Company respectively a "Notice on Ceasing the Listing and Transfer of Development Parcel 2002-005 in the Sea Area," which stated: "In accordance with the opinion of the Land Resources Department of Zhejiang Province, the Yuhuan Seaside New City Golden Harbor, i.e., development parcel number 2002-005 in the sea area, may not be listed and transferred until approved by the Provincial Department. Therefore, the Bureau ceases the listing and transfer of development parcel 2002-005 in the sea area. If the listing is resumed, a separate announcement will be made." On the same day, the Land Bureau refunded RMB 20,000,000 to Time Company. After receiving the above notice and funds, Time Company sent a "Reply to the Notice on Ceasing the Listing and Transfer of Development Parcel 2002-005 in the Sea Area" to the Land Bureau on December 6, 2002, stating: "Your Bureau's publication of the announcement and acceptance of the listing deposit and our company's listing quotation are civil legal acts that are legally binding on both parties. Your Bureau's arbitrary cessation of the listing has violated the relevant laws of our country and should be invalid. Our company now requests your Bureau to resume the listing and transfer the land according to law. If your Bureau persists in its actions, our company will lawfully request your Bureau to refund double the listing deposit and compensate for the corresponding economic losses. Please reply within five working days after receiving this letter; otherwise, our company will lawfully file a lawsuit against your Bureau."

Additionally: At the request of Time Company, the first instance court, on May 22, 2003, commissioned the Judicial Appraisal Division of the Zhejiang High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Appraisal Division) to appraise the following matters: 1. The authenticity of the letter dated November 20, 2002, setting the listing reserve price at RMB 57,000,000, i.e., whether the printed font and the seal of the Land Bureau on the letter were written or affixed on or before November 20, 2002; 2. Whether the printed font, handwritten font, and the seal of Yuhui Company on the "Listing Transfer Bid Quotation Form" dated November 21, 2002, were written or affixed on or before November 21, 2002. On June 27, 2003, the Appraisal Division issued a letter returning the case file, concluding that "the sample materials are insufficient and due to technical limitations, no appraisal conclusion can be made." Both parties had no objection to the letter, but Time Company argued that it should be sent to a more authoritative authority for appraisal and thus made another application.

On January 9, 2003, Time Company filed a lawsuit with the Zhejiang High People's Court, alleging: On November 7, 2002, the Land Bureau published the "Listing Transfer Announcement" in the "Yuhuan News," stating that, approved by the People's Government of Yuhuan County, the Land Bureau was listing and transferring the state-owned land use right for development parcel number 2002-005, with an area of 25.9434 hectares, intended use as mixed residential land, and a land use term of 70 years. Responding to the invitation to offer in the announcement, on November 20, 2002, Time Company submitted to the Land Bureau a copy of its business license showing a registered capital of RMB 100,890,000 and paid a listing deposit of RMB 20,000,000. On November 21, 2002, Time Company lawfully participated in the listing bidding at the Yuhuan County Real Estate Transaction Window, the designated listing location, and at 2:30 p.m. on the same day, posted a bid quotation form quoting RMB 50,000,000. On November 22, 2002, the Land Bureau, on the grounds that the development parcel had not been approved by the Land Resources Department of Zhejiang Province, notified Time Company to cease the listing and transfer of the parcel and refused to enter into a state-owned land use right transfer contract with Time Company. Time Company argued that according to national laws: "All types of commercial, tourism, entertainment, and commercial residential land must be transferred through bidding, auction, or listing." The Land Bureau, as the sole department authorized to transfer state-owned land on behalf of the state, published a listing announcement without approval from the competent authority and then canceled the listing, which was impossible under normal circumstances. The Land Bureau should bear full legal liability for this malicious breach of contract. Time Company had obtained the highest quotation in this listing and was the successful bidder. According to Article 29 of the Taizhou Municipal People's Government Decree No. 74, i.e., the "Administrative Measures for Bidding, Auction, and Listing of State-Owned Land Use Rights in Taizhou City" (hereinafter referred to as the Taizhou Municipal Government Decree), promulgated on November 11, 2001, the RMB 20,000,000 performance deposit paid by Time Company was a deposit for entering into a contract before the signing of the state-owned land use right transfer contract. Pursuant to Articles 89 and 90 of the "Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the Guarantee Law), the Land Bureau should refund double the deposit. According to the principle of fairness set forth in Article 4 of the "General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 5 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," and in line with the spirit of the "Notice on Strictly Implementing the Transfer of Commercial Land Use Rights through Bidding, Auction, or Listing" issued by the Ministry of Land and Resources and the Ministry of Supervision on August 26, 2002, in order to prevent the loss of state assets, the Land Bureau should not alter the conditions for the subject matter set forth in the "Listing Transfer Announcement" and the "Listing Transfer Instructions" and should promptly complete the relevant procedures and continue to fulfill the obligations set forth in the announcement. Therefore, Time Company requested: 1. An order that the Land Bureau continue to perform the contract and transfer the development parcel numbered 2002-005 to Time Company; 2. An order that the Land Bureau refund double the deposit paid by Time Company, which was designated as a deposit, amounting to RMB 4,000,000 (RMB 20,000,000 already refunded); 3. The Land Bureau to bear the case acceptance fee.

The Land Bureau defended, stating: 1. As to legal nature, the "Listing Transfer Announcement" dated November 7, 2002, was an invitation to offer directed at an unspecified majority, not an offer. Therefore, after issuing the announcement, the Land Bureau's revocation of the announcement upon the instruction of the Land Resources Department of Zhejiang Province was not a breach of contract, let alone a matter of continuing to perform the contract; 2. The Land Bureau's cessation of the listing and transfer of the development parcel was not out of malice but to comply with the instructions of the Land Resources Department of Zhejiang Province and procedural requirements. On November 21, 2002, the Land Bureau received not only the "Listing Transfer Bid Quotation Form" from Time Company but also one from Yuhui Company, and Time Company was not the highest bidder in this listing. After registering, Time Company immediately asked the Land Bureau for the listing materials. Due to the large number of people handling matters at the Land Bureau at the time, the staff could not attend to them promptly, and the Land Bureau requested Time Company to come back for the materials in 30 minutes, which led to unfounded suspicion from Time Company. Time Company immediately reported to the Land Resources Department of Zhejiang Province, alleging opaque operations by the Land Bureau. Given the report about this listing bidding, and because the listing and transfer of land without approval violated the relevant provisions of the "Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China," under the intervention of the Land Resources Department of Zhejiang Province, the Land Bureau issued the notice to cease the listing to Time Company. Thus, regarding the cessation of the listing, the Land Bureau had no malice; 3. Neither the "Listing Transfer Announcement" issued by the Land Bureau nor the administrative and institutional current accounts receipt issued by the Land Bureau clearly stated that the RMB 20,000,000 paid by Time Company on November 20, 2002, was merely a deposit, not a deposit for a contract. Time Company's characterization of the deposit as a contract deposit lacks legal basis. Therefore, the Land Bureau requested the dismissal of Time Company's claims.

The court of first instance found that, with respect to whether RMB 20 million was a deposit for earnest money or a deposit for security, according to Article 90 of the Security Law: "A deposit for earnest money shall be agreed in writing. The parties shall agree on the time for delivery of the deposit for earnest money in the deposit for earnest money contract. The deposit for earnest money contract shall take effect from the date of actual delivery of the deposit for earnest money." However, based on the evidence in this case, the parties did not enter into any form of deposit for earnest money contract or deposit for earnest money clause. From the relevant documents concerning the listed transfer, only a deposit of RMB 20 million was agreed upon. Furthermore, Article 118 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Interpretation on Security Law") provides: "Where a party delivers a lien deposit, guarantee deposit, earnest money deposit, contract deposit, security deposit, or deposit, but no deposit for earnest money nature is agreed, and the party claims the right of deposit for earnest money, the people's court shall not support it." According to this provision, Shijian Company's assertion of the right of deposit for earnest money lacks legal basis. "Agreement" refers to a consensus of intent between the parties, whereas the Order of the Taizhou Municipal Government is an administrative regulation independent of the parties' expression of intent. Accordingly, Shijian Company's argument that the content of the Taizhou Municipal Government Order constitutes the consensus of intent between the parties is untenable.

Regarding whether a state-owned land use right transfer contract was formed between the parties, Article 15, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law clearly provides: "An invitation to offer is an expression of intent to invite others to make an offer to oneself. Price lists, auction announcements, tender notices, prospectuses, commercial advertisements, etc., are invitations to offer." Accordingly, the listing announcement in this case constitutes an invitation to offer, not an offer. Shijian Company's allegation that this case involves an offer is untenable. On November 21, 2002, Shijian Company's quotation constituted an offer. According to Article 19 of the Provisions on the Transfer of State-Owned Land Use Rights by Tender, Auction, or Listing Promulgated by the Ministry of Land and Resources on May 9, 2002: "Upon expiration of the listing period, whether the transaction is concluded shall be determined in accordance with the following provisions: 1. If only one bidder quotes a price during the listing period, and the price is higher than the reserve price and meets other conditions, the listing transaction is concluded; 2. If two or more bidders quote prices during the listing period, the highest bidder shall be the winning bidder; if the prices are equal, the one who submits the quotation form first shall be the winning bidder, except where the price is lower than the reserve price; 3. If no bidder responds during the listing period or all bidders' quotations are lower than the reserve price or fail to meet other conditions, the listing transaction is not concluded. If two or more bidders request to quote at the expiration of the listing period, the transferor shall conduct on-site bidding for the listed parcel, and the highest bidder shall be the winning bidder." In this case, the Land Bureau, without prior approval in accordance with the law, listed and transferred the state-owned land use right without authorization. The Zhejiang Provincial Department of Land and Resources ordered the suspension of the listing. Under these circumstances, neither was Shijian Company determined to be the winning bidder, nor was a confirmation letter signed with it. The Land Bureau had not yet made an acceptance. Accordingly, the contractual relationship between the parties had not yet been formed. Shijian Company's allegation that a contractual relationship had been formed between the parties is untenable. Given that the letter of November 20, 2002, setting the reserve price for the listing at RMB 57 million and the "Listing Auction Quotation Form" of November 21, 2002, are not primary evidence in this case, their recognition or non-recognition does not affect the substantive handling of this case. Therefore, Shijian Company's request for a new appraisal of the above two pieces of evidence is not supported.

Regarding the validity of the state-owned land use right transfer contract between the parties, since the contractual relationship for the transfer of state-owned land use rights had not yet been formed, the issue of the validity of the transfer contract does not arise. As to the validity of this listing transfer itself, laws and regulations such as the Land Administration Law, the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Urban Real Estate Administration Law), the Regulations for the Implementation of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Regulations on the Development and Operation of Urban Real Estate do not stipulate the scope of authority for land transfer. However, Article 21 of the Implementation Measures of Zhejiang Province for the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, promulgated by the Standing Committee of the Zhejiang Provincial People's Congress and effective from July 5, 2000, provides: "Within the scope of approved conversion of agricultural land and within the scope of existing construction land, specific construction land shall be subject to examination and approval procedures in accordance with the following provisions: (1) For construction land projects of less than two hectares, the land administration department of the county (city) people's government shall review and submit to the same level people's government for approval, and report to the land administration department of the city with districts and the provincial people's government for record; (2) For construction land projects of two hectares or more but less than five hectares, the land administration department of the city with districts people's government shall review and submit to the same level people's government for approval, and report to the land administration department of the provincial people's government for record; among them, the people's governments of Hangzhou and Ningbo may approve construction land projects of two hectares or more but less than six hectares; (3) For construction land projects of six hectares or more in Hangzhou and Ningbo, and five hectares or more in other cities with districts, the land administration department of the provincial people's government shall review and submit to the provincial people's government for approval. Specific construction projects requiring the use of state-owned unused land designated in the overall land use plan shall go through examination and approval procedures in accordance with the preceding paragraph. Except as otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations." The disputed parcel in this case covers an area of 25.9434 hectares, which, according to the above provisions, should be submitted to the provincial government for approval. However, before the listing announcement, the Land Bureau did not submit for approval to the provincial government. Therefore, this listing act was also invalid. In summary, the court of first instance held that the listing act of the Land Bureau, having not been approved by the Zhejiang Provincial People's Government, was invalid; during the listing process, upon the order of the Zhejiang Provincial Department of Land and Resources, the Land Bureau stopped the listing act, did not confirm Shijian Company as the winning bidder, and did not accept Shijian Company's quotation. The contractual relationship between the parties had not yet been formed. Shijian Company's claim for a judgment ordering the parties to continue performing the contract and to transfer the disputed parcel to Shijian Company lacks legal basis and is not supported; the parties did not agree that the RMB 20 million paid by Shijian Company was a deposit for earnest money. Accordingly, Shijian Company's claim for double the return of the deposit for earnest money is not supported. Pursuant to Article 15 of the Contract Law, Article 90 of the Security Law, Article 118 of the Interpretation on Security Law, and Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: Shijian Company's claims are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 360,010 shall be borne by Shijian Company.

Shijian Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, alleging: The judgment of first instance was based on unclear facts, insufficient evidence, and erroneous application of law. It requested the revocation of the judgment of first instance, a ruling in favor of Shijian Company's claims, and an order that the Land Bureau bear the litigation costs of this case. The main facts and reasons are: (1) The judgment of first instance misstated the basic facts. Shijian Company should be the only legitimate bidder in this listing auction, but the Land Bureau fabricated the fact that a third party, Yuhui Company, participated in this listing auction. There was no reserve price for this listing transaction, and the Land Bureau colluded with the local notary office to issue a false reserve price certificate. Before the listing announcement, the Land Bureau had already signed a transfer contract with Yuhui Company regarding the land in question, and the listing announcement was "tailor-made" for Yuhui Company. (2) The judgment of first instance improperly applied the law. First, the judgment of first instance confused the legal relationship of the listing transfer with the legal relationship of the state-owned land use right transfer. Second, the listing transfer contractual relationship between Shijian Company and the Land Bureau had already been formed, and the Land Bureau's listing transfer of state-owned land use rights should be valid. Article 15, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law does not exclude the situation where a listing announcement constitutes an offer. This case's listing announcement explicitly stated that a contract would be concluded with the highest bidder, meeting all the requirements for constituting an offer under the Contract Law. Shijian Company was the only qualified bidder, and its quotation of RMB 50 million was higher than the starting price of RMB 43 million. In the absence of further bidding, this quotation constituted an effective acceptance of the Land Bureau's offer. The telephone notification from the Zhejiang Provincial Department of Land and Resources constituted an internal administrative act of the land and resources administrative system and did not affect the validity of the listing transfer legal relationship between the parties. According to the Urban Real Estate Administration Law, the disputed parcel in this case should be approved by the Yuhuan County People's Government, with the Land Bureau specifically implementing the transfer. Therefore, the Land Bureau was the only government body authorized to organize the implementation of the transfer of the disputed parcel, consistent with the legal provisions on the subject of land use right transfer. Pursuant to Article 4 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I), the court of first instance improperly used a local regulation promulgated by the Standing Committee of the Zhejiang Provincial People's Congress as the legal basis to determine that the listing act implemented by the Land Bureau was invalid. Third, after the transaction object and transaction price were determined through an effective listing act, the state-owned land use right transfer contract between the parties had already been formed, and the lack of approval from the relevant authorities rendered it a contract of pending validity. The court of first instance's view that the disputed parcel must be approved by the relevant authorities before listing and that the state-owned land use right transfer contract between the parties had not yet been formed lacks legal basis. Fourth, the deposit of RMB 20 million paid by Shijian Company to the Land Bureau during the listing transaction process should be legally characterized as a deposit for earnest money to secure contract formation. The judgment of first instance held that it was not a deposit for earnest money, which was an improper characterization. According to Article 29 of the Taizhou Municipal Government Order, the nature of the deposit in the transfer activities of state-owned land use rights within Taizhou City is a deposit for earnest money. This is the open and genuine expression of intent of the Taizhou Municipal Government as an equal civil subject in such activities, not a government act of promulgating administrative regulations as determined by the court of first instance. Pursuant to Article 118 of the Interpretation on Security Law, the deposit of RMB 20 million paid by Shijian Company is, in nature, a deposit for earnest money and should be subject to the relevant provisions of the Security Law on the penalty for deposit for earnest money. The purpose of the Land Bureau requiring Shijian Company to pay this RMB 20 million was to prevent Shijian Company from failing to enter into the transfer contract and pay the corresponding price after winning the bid. Furthermore, according to Article 60 of the Tendering and Bidding Law of the People's Republic of China, if a winning bidder refuses to sign a land transfer contract, the deposit is not refundable. Clearly, this deposit in this case has the nature of a deposit for earnest money to secure the formal conclusion of the contract. Therefore, the Land Bureau should continue to perform the contract; otherwise, it should bear the responsibility of returning double the deposit for earnest money.

The Land Bureau responded: The judgment of first instance was based on clear facts and correct application of law. It requested the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment. The main facts and reasons are: 1. Shijian Company was not the only legitimate bidder in this listing auction. Yuhui Company, which also met the bidder qualifications, submitted a quotation significantly higher than that of Shijian Company. Shijian Company's claim that the original documents and certificates provided by the relevant government departments were "forged" is unfounded. 2. There was a reserve price for this listing. Article 13 of the "Notice for Listing Auction" and the original reserve price document deposited by the Land Bureau with the Yuhuan County Notary Office fully demonstrate that before the listing, both parties had confirmed the existence of a reserve price for this listing and that the reserve price could not be fabricated afterwards. 3. According to the law, a listing announcement is an invitation to offer directed to unspecified persons. The Land Bureau could not accept Shijian Company's quotation, which was below the reserve price, nor could it sign a confirmation letter with Shijian Company. Therefore, Shijian Company's claim that a contract had been formed lacks factual and legal basis and cannot stand. 4. This listing was an act by the Land Bureau, as a government functional department, strictly in accordance with administrative regulations in conducting the transfer of state-owned land use rights. There is no issue of "tailor-making" the listing for Yuhui Company, as alleged by Shijian Company. The provisional contract signed between the Land Bureau and Yuhui Company was before the Ministry of Land and Resources promulgated the "Provisions on the Transfer of State-Owned Land Use Rights by Tender, Auction, or Listing." 5. The RMB 20 million deposit paid by Shijian Company cannot be interpreted as a deposit for earnest money with a security nature and should not be returned double. The listing announcement only stipulated that RMB 20 million was a performance deposit. The parties did not agree on the deposit for earnest money nature of the deposit, nor did they ever enter into any specific deposit for earnest money contract or clause. Article 29 of the Taizhou Municipal Government Order cannot serve as the legal basis for handling this case due to reasons such as lack of legislative authority and fundamentally different content nature. 6. The facts of this case do not meet the statutory circumstances for a contract of pending validity. The Land Bureau's listing and transfer of the disputed land without approval from the competent authority violated the provisions of the Land Administration Law and the Contract Law, and its listing act should be deemed invalid.

This Court, upon second instance trial, found that as of the conclusion of the second instance trial, the state-owned land use right transfer for the reclamation development area of Kanmen Yu Harbor Huajiao Reef in Zhugang Town, Yuhuan County, namely the development number 2002-005, had still not been approved by the Zhejiang Provincial People's Government.

During the second instance, Shijian Company submitted one new piece of evidence, namely the minutes of the executive meeting of the Yuhuan County People's Government ([2003] No. 4), to prove that the Land Bureau, while this case was still pending, was preparing to continue transferring the land in question to Yuhui Company by agreement, lacking even basic sincerity to fulfill its obligations under the listing. The Land Bureau argued that this evidence exceeded the time limit for submitting evidence and declined to provide cross-examination.

Other facts found by this Court in the second instance are substantially the same as those found by the court of first instance.

After the conclusion of the second instance trial, Shijian Company submitted a written application requesting a new appraisal of the authenticity of Yuhui Company's quotation form and the Land Bureau's reserve price form, and an investigation into whether Yuhui Company actually paid the deposit of RMB 20 million.

This Court holds that whether a state-owned land use right transfer contract relationship was formed between Shijian Company and the Land Bureau is a prerequisite for Shijian Company's request for continued performance of the contract and also the basis for the Land Bureau's contractual liability. The determination of this issue should be made by comprehensively considering three aspects: the legal nature of the listing announcement, whether there was an acceptance in this case, and the legal basis for the Land Bureau's liability. Regarding the legal nature of the listing announcement—whether it is an invitation to offer or an offer—the distinguishing standard should first be based on legal provisions. Article 15 of the Contract Law states that the legal nature of auction announcements and tender notices is an invitation to offer. The listing announcement published in the newspaper in this case is similar to auction announcements and tender notices; it is also an expression of intent directed to unspecified subjects to attract or invite the other party to make an offer. Its essence is to hope that bidders propose price terms, and its nature should be determined as an invitation to offer. Shijian Company's quotation on November 21, 2002, should be regarded as an offer in this case. Shijian Company's claim that the listing announcement itself constitutes an offer lacks legal basis and cannot stand. The Contract Law does not impose conditions on the withdrawal of an invitation to offer. After issuing an invitation to offer, if the offeror withdraws the invitation to offer, as long as it does not cause loss of reliance interests to a bona fide counterparty, the offeror generally does not bear legal liability. An invitation to offer does not form a contractual relationship, and its withdrawal also does not create contractual liability. Therefore, Shijian Company's claim that the Land Bureau should continue the listing and sign a state-owned land use right transfer contract with it lacks legal basis and is not supported. As to whether there was an acceptance in this case, on November 22, 2002, the day after Shijian Company and Yuhui Company had submitted their quotations but before bidding began, the Zhejiang Provincial Department of Land and Resources ordered the Land Bureau to stop the listing on the grounds of "listing and transferring state-owned land use rights without approval in accordance with the law." This caused the ongoing contracting process to be interrupted due to factual reasons. At that time, the bidding period of the listing process had not yet expired, the main terms of the state-owned land use right transfer contract—i.e., the price for the use right of the disputed parcel—had not been determined, and the Land Bureau had not accepted Shijian Company's quotation. The relationship between the parties remained at the offer stage in the process of concluding a contract. Therefore, the contract in this case had not been established due to lack of acceptance, and no contractual relationship was formed between the parties. Shijian Company's claim that there was an effective acceptance and that a contractual relationship had been formed between the parties is untenable. Since the contract in this case was not formed, Shijian Company's argument that there was a contract of pending validity between it and the Land Bureau is also not supported. Regarding the legal basis for the Land Bureau's liability, the ongoing state-owned land use right listing transaction in this case was not only unapproved at the time of the listing, but even by the conclusion of the second instance trial of this Court, the transfer of this state-owned land use right had still not been approved by the Zhejiang Provincial People's Government, thereby frustrating Shijian Company's purpose of entering into a state-owned land use right transfer contract. The Land Bureau is at fault and should bear corresponding pre-contractual liability. The loss of reliance interests incurred during the contracting stage must be protected through independent claims for compensation. During the second instance of this case, although the Land Bureau agreed to bear the compensation liability for pre-contractual fault, Shijian Company, up to the conclusion of the second instance trial, still insisted on the Land Bureau bearing the liability for continued performance of the contract or double the return of the deposit, and did not make a claim for compensation for losses caused by the Land Bureau's pre-contractual fault. Limited by the parties' claims and the scope of trial in second instance, this Court does not entertain this issue. Given that the contractual relationship between the parties in this case had not yet been formed, the judgment of first instance dismissing Shijian Company's claim for the Land Bureau to bear contractual liability is not improper in its application of law. As to whether the deposit of RMB 20 million stipulated in the "Listing Announcement" and the "Notice for Listing Auction" is a deposit for earnest money, the RMB 20 million was stated as a "deposit" in the "Listing Announcement" in this case, and the parties did not agree it was a deposit for earnest money. The Security Law and the Interpretation on Security Law provide the criteria for distinguishing between a deposit for earnest money and a deposit. That is, the precondition for a party to claim that a deposit is a deposit for earnest money is a clear agreement between the parties. Article 29 of the Taizhou Municipal Government Order, cited by Shijian Company, treats the deposit as a deposit for earnest money. However, since it is neither an agreement between the parties nor in accordance with relevant legal provisions, this government order cannot serve as the legal basis for determining that the RMB 20 million deposit in this case is a deposit for earnest money. The judgment of first instance correctly applied the law in holding that the RMB 20 million deposit in this case is not a deposit for earnest money. Shijian Company's claim that the RMB 20 million deposit should be a deposit for earnest money to secure formal contract formation and that the Land Bureau should return double the amount lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it. Shijian Company's requests during the second instance for a new appraisal of the authenticity of Yuhui Company's quotation form and the Land Bureau's reserve price form, and for an investigation into whether Yuhui Company actually paid the deposit of RMB 20 million, are not granted as they have no bearing on this Court's determination that the contract between the parties was not formed. In summary, the judgment of first instance was based on clear facts and correct application of law. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 360,010 is to be borne by Shijian Company in the amount of RMB 240,010 and by the Land Bureau in the amount of RMB 120,000.

This judgment is final.
